claims.value: Saint-Cyr says hunger drove the corps from its earlier positions toward Valls and supplies.
claims.rationale: Interested causal explanation attributed to the author, not accepted as a measured causal effect. English rendering (ours): "Famine, even more than the Spanish general’s dispositions, had forced the seventh corps to abandon its positions at Martorell, San Sadurni, Villa Franca and Vendrell."

claims.rationale: Saint-Cyr distinguishes Souham’s initial division from Pino’s later arrival but the checked pages provide no numerical local French return. Bodart’s whole-engagement figure is not an opening muster.

claims.value: Saint-Cyr describes Reding’s morning attack on Souham; Toreno describes Saint-Cyr’s later main crossing and assault. Both main attacks are retained across the day.
claims.rationale: Toreno’s page is printed 373 out of sequence between 336 and 338 (expected 337); IA leaf 342 identifies it unambiguously. These are main successive attacks, not merely countercharges. English rendering (ours): "He rushed the post and immediately attacked Souham’s division; [Saint-Cyr] crossed the Francoli and assaulted the height where our troops had repositioned."

citations.locator: saint-cyr, printed p. 121, Internet Archive leaf 125; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: il brusqua ce poste et attaqua de suite la division Souham

claims.value: Saint-Cyr describes Souham sending for guidance, the chief ordering pursuit and bringing Pino’s division to Valls.
claims.rationale: Local morning Souham action versus Saint-Cyr’s subsequent combined direction. English rendering (ours): "The chief ordered him to do so and said he would immediately gather the Italian division and move onto the Tarragona road."

citations.locator: saint-cyr, printed p. 121, Internet Archive leaf 125; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Le général en chef le lui ordonna, et lui fit dire qu’il allait de suite réunir la division italienne et se porter sur la route de Tarragone.

claims.value: Toreno places Castro over the Spanish right and Marti over the left and centre, within Reding’s field army.
claims.rationale: Sector tasks, not automatic additional commander credit. English rendering (ours): "Castro directed the Spanish right; the left and centre remained under General Marti."

claims.value: Saint-Cyr describes the Francoli’s steep difficult banks fronting the Spanish position.
claims.rationale: Author’s qualitative appraisal attributed; no defensive score. English rendering (ours): "The Francoli, whose steep difficult banks gave the Spaniards an admirable position to defend."
